I am a 50-year-old rice farmer in Nigeria's North Central region. I have no formal schooling, but I have been farming this land for many years. My household owns this 0.58-hectare rice plot, and I manage a total of 1.27 hectares across my farm. I need to decide how to manage this plot for the coming season.

I have thought carefully about this season. Chemical fertilizer is expensive and hard to get, and I worry it will harm my soil over time, so I will not use it this year. However, I have saved some manure from my livestock, and I will spread that on the plot to help the rice grow strong. I always use our traditional seed — it is what my father used, and I trust it more than those new hybrid seeds that cost too much and do not always do well here. I will not spray pesticides or herbicides because they are costly and I prefer to weed by hand with my family. Water is a problem in this region, and I have no irrigation system, so I depend on the rains; I cannot irrigate. My wife, children, and I will work this plot together — we expect about 45 days of family labor over the season. I do not have money to hire outside workers, so all the work will be done by my household.
